generations.prompt: A wide, still shot of an old woman sitting alone on the porch of a weathered timber house in warm late-afternoon sun, a small cloth-covered device on the table beside her. She looks down at the device and talks to it easily, the way you talk to an old friend. She speaks a soft, unfamiliar, vowel-rich language of her own, not English, with the stress late in each word. She says, unhurried: "Noréla tové seli ené." (no-réh-la toh-véh seh-lee eh-néh). Then she gives a small dry laugh and looks out at the field. The device's small amber light glows steadily. Tall grass moves in a light wind. Sound: her voice, wind in dry grass, a few insects, a porch board creaking. The camera is locked off and does not move. No music. No subtitles, captions or on-screen text of any kind.
